hero.lead: A landlocked nation of 7.9 million on the Mekong, whose rivers power two thirds of its grid and much of its exports, with public debt of 88.8% of GDP and only one household in ten cooking with clean fuel.

capital.heading: Rivers of power, and a heavy debt.

register.name: US$500 million 9.625% notes due 2032
register.detail: Lao People’s Democratic Republic · senior unsecured · Rule 144A and Regulation S · listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange, listing ceremony 29 October 2026 · 50% of principal repaid one year before maturity
register.note: Orders of 2.9 times the amount offered, from 86 investors; the first Lao government bond included in the Emerging Markets Bond Index (EMBI)
register.text: The largest international offering by the Lao government to date: senior unsecured notes of US$500 million at a coupon of 9.625%, due in 2032. The listing supports the Government’s efforts to diversify its financing options and improve debt management. It serves the public finances behind all seven standards.

register.name: US$300 million 11.25% notes due 2030
register.detail: Lao People’s Democratic Republic, represented by the Ministry of Finance · Rule 144A and Regulation S · listed on the Singapore Exchange · announced 24 November 2025
register.note: Proceeds for the Government’s debt management and general budgetary needs
register.text: International notes of US$300 million at a coupon of 11.25%, due in 2030 and offered to institutional investors. The proceeds support the Government’s debt management and general budgetary needs, the public finances behind all seven standards.

register.name: First CNY-denominated government bonds
register.detail: Government of the Lao PDR · issued December 2024 · CNY273.2 million · listed on the Lao Securities Exchange in January 2025
register.note: Local currency government bonds outstanding were LAK29.8 trillion at the end of 2024
register.text: The Government’s first bonds denominated in Chinese yuan, worth US$37.4 million and listed on the Lao Securities Exchange. They widen the sources of finance for the state budget, which carries the seven standards.

register.name: Improving Frontline Workers Performance in Education and Health
register.detail: World Bank · IDA · approved 14 January 2026 · six years · P507442
register.note: District hospitals and health centres in eight target provinces
register.text: A six-year project to build continuous professional development for teachers, with classroom observation, learning assessments and smart classrooms in teacher training colleges, and to strengthen the registration, licensing, training and retention of health workers. It serves the education and health standards, with measures to attract and keep staff in rural and underserved areas.

register.name: Enhancing Public Financial Management through ICT and Skills Project
register.detail: World Bank · IDA low-interest loan · approved 7 November 2025 · second phase · P510862
register.note: An integrated financial management information system and training for spending units at all levels of government
register.text: A low-interest loan from the International Development Association for the second phase of the integrated financial management information system, with training for staff of spending units at all levels of government. Clearer budget planning, implementation and reporting serve the public finances behind all seven standards.

register.name: REDD+ results-based payments, Southern Laos (FP282)
register.detail: Green Climate Fund · approved at the 43rd Board meeting, 29 October 2025 · results period 2015 to 2018 · accredited entity JICA
register.note: USD 61,465,393 for the Governance, Forest Landscapes and Livelihoods – Southern Laos Project (GFLL-SL)
register.text: Results-based payments for emission reductions from reduced deforestation and forest degradation achieved in Laos from 2015 to 2018. They finance national REDD+ coordination and better governance, forest landscapes and livelihoods in the Southern region, which serves the livelihood standard.

register.name: Climate Resilient Road Connectivity Improvement Project
register.detail: World Bank · Approved 30 September 2024
register.text: Roads that survive the monsoon.

register.name: Lao Health and Nutrition Services Access Project II
register.detail: World Bank · Approved 21 February 2024
register.text: Health and nutrition services for mothers and children.

register.name: Reducing Rural Poverty and Malnutrition Project II
register.detail: World Bank · Approved 30 November 2023
register.text: Nutrition and livelihoods in rural villages.

register.name: Responsible Forestry Project, Phase I
register.detail: ADB · approved 18 December 2025 · $5 million concessional loan from ordinary capital resources · $5 million Asian Development Fund grant
register.text: The first phase of a programme to halt forest degradation, strengthen climate resilience and improve the livelihoods of forest-dependent communities, through partnerships of government, private investors and communities for commercial plantations and conservation. It prepares the feasibility studies for Phase II and serves the livelihood standard.

register.name: Skills Enhancement for Inclusive and Green Economic Development Project
register.detail: ADB · approved 21 November 2025 · $30 million concessional ordinary capital resources · $3 million Asian Development Fund grant · $3 million grant from the Japan Fund for Prosperous and Resilient Asia and the Pacific
register.note: Eleven schools upgraded, with modern dormitories for rural girls
register.text: A package to align technical and vocational education and training with the labour market, with courses in e-vehicle maintenance, ICT and industrial electrical work, teacher training, stipends for returning students and climate-resilient upgrades of 11 schools. It serves the education and livelihood standards, with a focus on jobs for young people, particularly women.

register.name: Green Primary Care Project
register.detail: ADB · announced 11 September 2025 · $30 million ordinary capital resources · $10 million Asian Development Fund · $1 million technical assistance from the Community Resilience Partnership Program Trust Fund
register.note: 51 districts in Champasak, Louangphabang, Oudomxai, Savannakhet and Xiangkhouang
register.text: A package to upgrade and equip primary care facilities, train health workers to keep services running in extreme weather, upgrade water systems and carry out community climate adaptation plans. It serves the health and water standards in 51 districts, 14 of them climate-vulnerable.

register.name: Sustainable Agrifood Systems Sector Project
register.detail: ADB · announced 7 July 2025 · $50 million in loans from ADB, the ASEAN Infrastructure Fund and the EU-ASEAN Catalytic Green Finance Facility · $15.8 million in grants
register.note: Grants from the Asian Development Fund, the Green Climate Fund and the High-Level Technology Fund
register.text: Investments in financial services, technical services, small-scale infrastructure and food safety for climate resilience, food security, nutrition and incomes, with value added to bamboo, coffee, durian, cassava and tea before export. Financial services reach the whole nation, and technical services and infrastructure six provinces in the north and south; it serves the food and livelihood standards.

register.name: Domestic Resource Mobilization Modernization Project
register.detail: ADB · Loan 4530-LAO, concessional ordinary capital resources · approved 8 November 2024 · signed 12 December 2024 · with $2 million of technical assistance
register.note: Digital taxpayer services, e-invoicing and a tax academy
register.text: A concessional ADB loan to modernise tax administration, with digital taxpayer services, computerised accounting and e-invoicing systems, stronger data analytics and a tax academy. More efficient and transparent tax collection serves the public finances behind all seven standards.

register.name: National Road 13 South Extension Improvement and Maintenance Project
register.detail: AIIB · sovereign-backed · financing approved 6 November 2024 · co-financed by the Abu Dhabi Fund for Development and the Government · 10-year performance-based road contract
register.note: A project preparation grant of $1 million, approved 30 April 2025, prepares the next sections of the road
register.text: Improves, rehabilitates and maintains a 50 km section of National Road 13, from KM21 near Vientiane to KM71 in Bolikhamxay province, widening the first 20 km from two lanes to four. Reliable roads to markets and services bear on the livelihood standard.

register.name: Australian development assistance to Laos, 2026-27
register.detail: Australian Government · total official development assistance, budget estimate · bilateral allocation A$26.1 million · A$55.1 million in 2025-26 · A$55.8 million actual in 2024-25
register.note: Programmes include BEQUAL 2 for basic education (A$33.3 million, 2022 to 2026) and Driving Down Dengue (A$7.5 million, 2024 to 2028)
register.text: Australia’s total official development assistance to Laos estimated for 2026-27, up from A$55.1 million in 2025-26, under the Development Partnership Plan 2024-2029. Its programmes for basic education and health serve the education and health standards.

register.name: Project for the Improvement of the Referral Hospital in the Southern Region
register.detail: JICA grant agreement · signed 9 January 2026 · Champasak Provincial Hospital · signed for Laos by the Ministry of Finance
register.note: Maximum amount; a new central clinical building with emergency, surgical and intensive care units
register.text: A Japanese grant to build a new central clinical building at Champasak Provincial Hospital, with emergency and surgical departments and an Intensive Care Unit, and to procure and install medical equipment. It strengthens referral care in the southern region and serves the health standard.

register.name: 300-bed state hospital in Vientiane
register.detail: Korea EDCF loan · construction began September 2025 · about 2.5 years to complete · overseen by the Ministry of Public Security
register.note: Advanced equipment and units for infectious diseases and mental health
register.text: A loan from Korea’s Economic Development Cooperation Fund for a modern state-owned hospital of 300 beds in Vientiane, to meet growing demand for quality healthcare. It serves the health standard.

register.name: Project for the Improvement of the Provincial Teacher Development Centers
register.detail: JICA grant agreement · signed 25 February 2025, Vientiane · nine provinces
register.note: Maximum amount; Phongsaly, Oudomxay, Bokeo, Houaphanh, Xayabury, Borikhamxai, Khammouane, Sekong and Attapeu
register.text: A Japanese grant to build and equip Provincial Teacher Development Centers in nine provinces, with consulting services. Better training for teachers serves the education standard, the one furthest from reach in Laos.

register.name: Global Gateway package for Lao PDR, 2025 to 2027
register.detail: European Union · announced 31 January 2025, Vientiane · entirely in grants · green and inclusive economy, human capital, good governance
register.note: Human capital covers education, including technical and vocational training, and healthcare
register.text: A new allocation of €45 million in grants for 2025 to 2027, in three priority areas: a green and inclusive economy, human capital and good governance. It covers sustainable agriculture and rural development, education, healthcare and public financial management, and so serves the food, education, health and livelihood standards.

assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.name: The Clean Grid
items.label: Of electricity from renewable sources, 2021
items.text: Dams on the Mekong and its tributaries: two thirds of the power.

items.name: The Forest
items.label: Of the land under forest, 2024
items.text: Forest across more than half the land.

items.name: The Fresh Water
items.label: Renewable fresh water a person, 2022
items.text: More than 25,000 cubic metres of fresh water a person each year.

items.name: The Minerals
items.label: Of GDP from mineral rents, 2021
items.text: Metals and minerals already earn; the task is to keep more of their value at home.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: 29.8% are under fifteen: the workforce and the market of the next generation.

items.name: Big Brother Mouse
items.text: A Lao-owned not-for-profit that publishes books in the Lao language and runs schools whose modest tuition fees cover basic costs such as teacher salaries; it has 12 schools with 4,200 students, and its Little Elephant school, a preschool since September 2023 with 388 children enrolled, opened a six-room primary school in September 2025.

items.name: Ock Pop Tok
items.text: An artisan social enterprise in Luang Prabang, founded in 2000 and run by women, that sells Lao textiles and crafts through its shops, webshop, weaving classes, café and villa, and works with more than 500 artisans throughout Laos.

items.name: Women With Disability Association (WWDA)
items.text: An organisation founded by Chanhpheng Sivila, at work since 2001 and an association since 2021, that trains women with disabilities in weaving, pottery, ceramics and paper crafts, sells their handicrafts to foreign buyers and helps them into jobs; nearly 30 students from Oudomxay and Bokeo provinces were enrolled at its centre in 2025.

items.name: Xon Phao
items.text: A social enterprise in Vientiane, created in 2017, that employs people with disabilities to make handicraft gifts based on traditional Lao weaving and sells them through the XonPhao Shop and to buyers abroad; about 30 people worked there in 2021.

items.name: Vanmai Coffee Cooperative
items.text: A coffee cooperative in Houaphanh province, where coffee was introduced as a sustainable alternative to opium cultivation, which is building a warehouse and secondary processing facilities with UNDP and UNODC from November 2024 to September 2027, so that its producers can sell value-added coffee in domestic and international markets.
